answer: Each identity locks a 75-credit bond and crosses a ledge of four verified jobs. Each receipt bears a quartz seal, and a mirror copy goes to a ledger. An auditor checks the mirror against the originals; a missing job, reused receipt, or seal mismatch burns the bond. The first pays 24 per job, 96 total. The k-th identity from one funder pays 24+3(k-1) per job, so the 1000th pays 12084, and 1000 fakes pay 6090000 plus 75000 locked. A mirror-copy ring fails because a quartz seal cannot be resealed under a second key. An honest agent pays 75 plus 96, then recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
